title: Line-bundle cohomology for a rational tail or bridge contraction
statement: Let $T$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $Y\to T$ and $X\to T$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], finitely presented families of nonempty connected reduced nodal curves of pure dimension one [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres]. Here finitely presented includes quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Let $q:Y\to X$ be a $T$-morphism such that on each geometric fibre it is either an isomorphism, or contracts one component $A\simeq\mathbf P^1$ to a point and is an isomorphism off $A$. Assume in the latter case that $A$ meets the closure of its complement in one or two distinct transverse nodes. Let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Suppose $\deg(\mathcal L|_A)\geq-1$ for every contracted geometric component, with degree as in [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. Then $q_*\mathcal L$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent] and of finite presentation (locally the cokernel of a map between finite rank free modules), is flat over $T$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], and $R^1 q_*\mathcal L=0$, where $R^i q_*$ denotes the right derived functor of direct image of structure-sheaf modules [pqf-def-cohomology]. For every $h:T'\to T$, write $X'=X\times_TT'$, $Y'=Y\times_TT'$, $q':Y'\to X'$ and $h_X,h_Y$ for the projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. The canonical map $h_X^*q_*\mathcal L\to q'_*h_Y^*\mathcal L$ is an isomorphism. If every contracted degree is nonnegative, the adjunction evaluation $q^*q_*\mathcal L\to\mathcal L$ is surjective [def-pc-module-pullback]. These base-change comparisons commute with composition and with isomorphisms of the diagrams and line bundles.

source.place: Section 1, Corollary 1.5 (printed p.167), conditions (1)--(2) and conclusions (i)--(iv); application to contractions on pp.167--168. Arbitrary-base finite-presentation form, with exceptional degrees at least -1; local PDF WANTED, primary-author scan p.167 consulted online.

proof.text: The morphism $X\to T$ is separated since it is proper. Apply the proper-to-separated-target theorem to $Y\to T$ and $q:Y\to X$ to obtain that $q$ is proper. The module $\mathcal L$ is quasi-coherent and finitely presented because locally it is $\mathcal O_Y$; at each $y$, its stalk is free of rank one over $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. That stalk is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ by flatness of $Y\to T$, so $\mathcal L$ is flat over $T$. Thus the diagram and module hypotheses of the relative acyclic direct-image criterion are satisfied; its fibre hypotheses are checked next.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, and view it as an $\Omega$-rational point on $X_\Omega$ for the resulting geometric base point of $T$. If $q_\Omega$ is an isomorphism, or if $x$ lies away from its contracted image, its scheme-theoretic fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Otherwise the reduced fibre is the component $A\cong\mathbf P^1_\Omega$. The map $Y_\Omega\to X_\Omega$ is proper and surjective: it maps onto the contracted point and is an isomorphism on its complement. Both curves are proper, reduced and of pure dimension one; $A$ is nonempty and connected, and its ambient neighbourhood is nodal. At a smooth target point the local ring is essentially smooth over $\Omega$, Noetherian, and has residue field $\Omega$. The smooth-over-field differential-dimension theorem gives cotangent dimension one, since the fibre curve has pure dimension one. The smooth rational-point completion theorem then gives completed local ring $\Omega[[t]]$. At a nonsmooth target point the nodal hypothesis gives completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. In these two cases we obtain precisely the ordinary $n$-fold points of the nodal-contraction normalization-branches theorem with $n=1$ and $n=2$, respectively. Its reduced-fibre clause therefore gives $Y_x=(Y_x)_{\mathrm{red}}=A$ as schemes. In every case the geometric fibre of $q$ has dimension at most one; no infinitesimal thickening of $A$ is being discarded.

proof.text: On a projective-line fibre, classification gives $\mathcal L|_A\cong\mathcal O_A(d)$ for some integer $d$. The monomial cohomology formula with $n=1$ gives $\chi(\mathbf P^1,\mathcal O(d))=d+1$ for all $d$: for $d\geq0$ there are $d+1$ degree-zero monomials and none in degree one; for $d=-1$ both groups are zero; for $d\leq-2$ there are $-d-1$ degree-one monomials and none in degree zero. All higher groups vanish. Also $\chi(\mathcal O)=1$. Consequently the definition of degree gives $\deg(\mathcal L|_A)=d$. The assumption is therefore $d\geq-1$, and the same formula gives $H^1(A,\mathcal L|_A)=0$. On a point fibre, an invertible module is one-dimensional and has zero positive cohomology (the $n=0$ case of the formula). This verifies the cohomology hypothesis on every geometric fibre, including the identity case.

proof.text: Apply the relative acyclic direct-image criterion with $(S,U,V,f,\mathcal F)=(T,Y,X,q,\mathcal L)$. Step 1 supplied its properness, flatness and finite-presentation hypotheses and steps 2--3 its geometric-fibre dimension and cohomology hypotheses. It gives that $q_*\mathcal L$ is quasi-coherent, finitely presented and $T$-flat, that $R^1q_*\mathcal L=0$, and that its canonical comparison $h_X^*q_*\mathcal L\to q'_*h_Y^*\mathcal L$ is an isomorphism for every $T'\to T$. The criterion assumes no Noetherian condition and requires no flatness of $q$ or of $h$.

proof.text: Suppose now all contracted degrees are nonnegative. In step 3 the integer $d$ on each projective-line fibre is then nonnegative. The homogeneous polynomials $x_0^d$ and $x_1^d$ give global sections of $\mathcal O(d)$, and on $U_0$ the first is a basis section while on $U_1$ the second is a basis section, by the standard twisting transition relation. Thus these two sections generate; when $d=0$ the section $1$ suffices. A one-dimensional module on $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is also generated by its global sections. Every geometric fibre therefore satisfies the generation condition of the same relative criterion. Its evaluation conclusion gives the asserted surjection $q^*q_*\mathcal L\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal L$.

proof.text: The maps just used are canonical, not choices of the projective-line identifications. Explicitly, locally on an affine $W\subseteq X$ and an affine $W'\subseteq X'$ mapping to it, the base-change map sends a local tensor $b'\otimes s$, for $s\in\Gamma(q^{-1}W,\mathcal L)$, to $b' h_Y^*s$ on $q'^{-1}W'$. For a further base change, both the direct map and the composite send $b''\otimes(b'\otimes s)$ to $b''h^*(b')\,(h_Y\circ h'_Y)^*s$ under the tensor associativity identification. They are equal on generators and hence equal as sheaf maps. For an isomorphism of diagrams and a compatible line-bundle isomorphism $u$, both naturality paths send that tensor to the pullback of $b'$ times the pullback of $u(s)$; restriction to smaller affine opens gives the same formula. This proves compatibility with composition and with isomorphisms. Evaluation itself sends $a\otimes s$ to $a s$, so its compatibility follows by the same product formula. These computations also show that the auxiliary noncanonical fibre identifications in steps 2--3 do not alter any asserted comparison.
